extracted.intended_audience: writers submitting fiction or humor to McSweeney's Quarterly Concern (print) or McSweeney's Internet Tendency (web)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for submitting short fiction and humor to McSweeney's print Quarterly Concern and the web-based Internet Tendency, including venue expectations, formatting/length guidance, and content/style qualities the editors favor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue focus — McSweeney's Quarterly Concern (print)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mostly fiction; some nonfiction; rarely poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "There are no rules" — the best test is to read the Quarterly; the Quarterly favors literary ambition and formats that reward close reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict no-AI policy
rubrics_metrics.description: McSweeney's accepts no writing aided in any manner by AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions must be wholly human-authored; any AI assistance disqualifies a submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission method
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions must be sent via the Submittable platform; other methods will not be accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue focus — McSweeney's Internet Tendency (web)
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor and satire, not traditional fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on conceptual humor pieces rather than straight literary short fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count limit (Internet Tendency)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the stated maximum; shorter pieces (under 1,000 words) are preferred for the web humor venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common web formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet Tendency often publishes list-format, parody-format, voice-driven monologues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conceptual or formally distinct presentations (lists, parodies, monologues) are commonly successful on the site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinctive voice — often funny and a little weird.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong, individual narrative voice is prized; voice should carry the piece and contribute to its humor or strangeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual hook
rubrics_metrics.description: The piece 'is about' something at multiple levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful submissions have a conceptual core or hook that operates both on the surface and at deeper levels (conceptual humor).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression
rubrics_metrics.description: Every line must earn its keep.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economy of language is important; avoid filler and ensure each sentence contributes to voice, joke, or story progression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tonal control
rubrics_metrics.description: Humor should not tip into smugness or meanness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a tone that is funny without alienating readers; balance edge with empathy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary ambition (Quarterly)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Quarterly rewards work with literary ambition and that benefits from close reading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even unconventional formats should offer depth, craft, and rewards for attentive readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality of form
rubrics_metrics.description: McSweeney's has historically published unconventional forms (epistolary, footnoted, fragmented, list, recipe-format, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Innovative or formally unusual presentations are welcome, provided they serve the piece and readers can engage with them.
